title: The Domain of the Body
coreMove: Stillness needs a cared-for body: lower the noise, make recovery easy, and stop treating rest, movement, and leisure as rewards earned after collapse.

exampleSpecs.audience: people who treat exhausted bodies as a scheduling inconvenience
exampleSpecs.stakes: treat recovery as part of judgment, not a perk
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Dalia delays a noncritical translation block until a rested interpreter rotates in

exampleSpecs.audience: people who treat speed as the only serious route
exampleSpecs.stakes: make relaxation in nature practical after bodily strain
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Rene chooses the courtyard exit before reopening work

exampleSpecs.audience: leaders who confuse urgency with accuracy
exampleSpecs.stakes: show errors falling after the body settles
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Kira sees accuracy improve after the crew gets a short outdoor reset

exampleSpecs.audience: people whose tired intentions need a visible setup
exampleSpecs.stakes: make bodily philosophy easier than another work loop
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Joss sets up lunch, water, and one quiet page before returning to class

exampleSpecs.audience: people whose bodies warn them before skill collapses
exampleSpecs.stakes: reset a punishing routine before effort becomes unsafe
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Camila rewrites the lift sequence when her hands start shaking

exampleSpecs.audience: people who pretend judgment floats above the body
exampleSpecs.stakes: show posture, water, light, and breaks shaping perception
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Beatrice sees that missed notes are body data, not just skill data
